tool.name: Bismark Methylation Extractor
tool.command:
python '$__tool_directory__/bismark_methylation_extractor.py'
--multicore \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} --infile '$input'
#if $singlePaired.sPaired == "single": --single-end #if $singlePaired.ignore_r1 != 0: --ignore '$singlePaired.ignore_r1' #end if #if $singlePaired.ignore_3prime_r1 != 0: --ignore_3prime '$singlePaired.ignore_3prime_r1' #end if #else: --paired-end #if $singlePaired.no_overlap: --no-overlap #end if #if $singlePaired.ignore_r1 != 0: --ignore '$singlePaired.ignore_r1' #end if #if $singlePaired.ignore_3prime_r1 != 0: --ignore_3prime '$singlePaired.ignore_3prime_r1' #end if #if $singlePaired.ignore_r2 != 0: --ignore_r2 '$singlePaired.ignore_r2' #end if #if $singlePaired.ignore_3prime_r2 != 0: --ignore_3prime_r2 '$singlePaired.ignore_3prime_r2' #end if #end if
#if $splitting_report: --splitting_report '$output_splitting_report' #end if #if $mbias_report: --mbias_report '$output_mbias_report' #end if
#if $cytosine_report_selector.cytosine_report: --cytosine_report '$output_cytosine_report' #if $cytosine_report_selector.coverage_output: --coverage_file '$coverage_file' #end if
#if $cytosine_report_selector.refGenomeSource.genomeSource == "built_in_fasta": --genome_file '$cytosine_report_selector.refGenomeSource.built_in_fasta.fields.path' #else: --genome_file '$cytosine_report_selector.refGenomeSource.genome_file' #end if
#if not $cytosine_report_selector.cpg_context: --cx_context #end if #end if
#if $output_settings.comprehensive: --comprehensive #end if #if $output_settings.merge_non_cpg: --merge-non-cpg #end if --compress '$compressed_output'
#if $output_settings.separate_logfile: --log_report '$log_report' #end if

param.name: input
param.label: Submit the resulting bam/sam file from Bismark bisulfite mapper

param.name: sPaired
param.label: Is this library mate-paired?

param.name: ignore_r1
param.label: Ignore the first N bases from the 5' end of read 1
param.help: Ignore the first N bases from the 5' end of each read when processing methylation calls, e.g. to compensate for biased methylation figures at the extreme 5' end of reads as a result of end-repair. Default: 0.

param.name: ignore_3prime_r1
param.label: Ignore the last N bases from the 3' end of read 1
param.help: Ignore the last N bases from the 3' end of each read when processing methylation calls. Default: 0.

param.name: no_overlap
param.label: Disable overlapping of paired-end reads
param.help: We do not overlap paired-end reads since default behaviour of methylation extractor is to not overlap. Overlapping was default in Bismark versions before v0.7.0

param.name: ignore_r1
param.label: Ignore the first N bases from the 5' end of read 1
param.help: Ignore the first N bases from the 5' end of each read when processing methylation calls, e.g. to compensate for biased methylation figures at the extreme 5' end of reads as a result of end-repair. Default: 0.

param.name: ignore_3prime_r1
param.label: Ignore the last N bases from the 3' end of read 1
param.help: Ignore the last N bases from the 3' end of each read when processing methylation calls. Default: 0.

param.name: ignore_r2
param.label: Ignore the first N bases from the 5' end of read 2
param.help: Ignore the first N bases from the 5' end of each read when processing methylation calls, e.g. to compensate for biased methylation figures at the extreme 5' end of reads as a result of end-repair. Default: 0.

param.name: ignore_3prime_r2
param.label: Ignore the last N bases from the 3' end of read 2
param.help: Ignore the last N bases from the 3' end of each read when processing methylation calls. Default: 0.

param.name: splitting_report
param.label: Output a splitting report

param.name: mbias_report
param.label: Output a M-bias report

param.name: cytosine_report
param.label: Do you want to output a cytosine report?
param.help: The methylation extractor outputs a cytosine methylation report which includes all cytosines in the reads, irrespective of whether they were methylated or not. The output file has the following format: chromosome, start, end, methylation call, number of reads supporting the methylation call, percent methylation.
param.option: No, do not output cytosine report
Yes, I want a cytosine report

param.name: genomeSource
param.label: Will you select a reference genome from your history or use a built-in index?
param.help: Built-ins were indexed using default options
param.option: Use reference genome (fasta) from my Galaxy history

param.name: built_in_fasta
param.label: Select reference genome (fasta)

param.name: genome_file
param.label: Select the reference genome

param.name: cpg_context
param.label: Do you want the output to be CpG context only?
param.help: The default is to output cytosines in any context (CpG, CHG or CHH). If you want to exclude non-CpG cytosines, select this option.

param.name: coverage_output
param.label: Do you want to output a coverage file?
param.help: The methylation extractor outputs an additional file which contains the coverage (number of reads) for each cytosine in the genome.

param.name: comprehensive
param.label: Use --comprehensive
param.help: The default methylation extractor output files are 8 individual files depending on the context (CpG, CHG or CHH) and strand (OT, CTOT, OB or CTOB). Using this option will merge these files into one single file per context.

param.name: merge_non_cpg
param.label: Use --merge_non_CpG
param.help: Merges the CHG and CHH contexts into one non-CpG context.

param.name: separate_logfile
param.label: Create a separate logfile, otherwise logs are added to the dataset info.

tool.help:
**What it does**
The Bismark Methylation Extractor reads in a bisulfite read alignment Bismark mapping output file and extracts the methylation calls for every single cytosine in the genome.
The extracted methylation calls can be written out in a context-dependent (CpG, CHG or CHH) manner, and the strand origin of every alignment is taken into account.
-----
**Output formats**
The methylation extractor produces one output file per library (or per strand orientation if the option *--comprehensive* was not used). The extracted methylation calls are written out in the following format:
The first 4 columns are identical to a standard SAM/BAM file: read-ID, methylation state of the alignment (OT, CTOT, OB, CTOB), chromosome and position of the cytosine. The 5th column contains the methylation call itself:
- `Z` — methylated C in CpG context - `z` — unmethylated C in CpG context - `X` — methylated C in CHG context - `x` — unmethylated C in CHG context - `H` — methylated C in CHH context - `h` — unmethylated C in CHH context
The strand origin of every alignment is taken into account, i.e. alignments to the original top strand (OT), complementary to original top strand (CTOT), original bottom strand (OB) and complementary to original bottom strand (CTOB) are written to separate output files unless *--comprehensive* is selected.
**Methylation context**
- `--comprehensive` — merges the four strand-specific files into one per context - `--merge_non_CpG` — merges the CHG and CHH contexts into one non-CpG context - `--cytosine_report` — outputs the methylation state of every single cytosine in the genome (requires the reference genome) - `--CX_context` — includes non-CpG cytosines in the cytosine report (default is CpG only)
-----
**More information**
For more information please take a look at the Bismark documentation at https://felixkrueger.github.io/Bismark/.
